tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumulum: tumulus, -ī (m.) — mound, hillock, burial mound (acc. sg.)
tuos: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m. acc. pl.)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
unaque: ūnā (adv.) — together, at the same time, in one company + -que, and
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
variis: varius, -a, -um — varied, many-coloured, diverse (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
vasto: vastus, -a, -um — vast, huge, desolate (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
vel: vel (conj., adv.) — or; even; vel… vel, either… or
velle: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, want, be willing (pres. inf.)
velut: velut (adv.) — as, just as, as if
venientum: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (pres. part., gen. pl. = venientium)
ventura: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come; ventūrus, about to come; ventūra (n. pl.), things to come (fut. part., n. acc. pl.)
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
veterumque: vetus, -eris — old, ancient; veterēs, forefathers, ancestors (m. gen. pl.) + -que, and
vides: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. pres.)
videt: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. pres.)
vires: vīs (f.) — force; pl. vīrēs, strength (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (fractae vīrēs)
virgulta: virgultum, -ī (n.) — brushwood, shrub, shoots (nom./acc. pl.; usually plural)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
visu: vīsus, -ūs (m.) — sight, seeing (abl. sg.; miserābile vīsū, pitiable to see)
vita: vīta, -ae (f.) — life, living; the breath of life (nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
volvere: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, turn; to pass through, undergo (pres. inf.)
